The sampling plan is intended to enable the discovery of unbiased and reliable estimates of 
monitored parameter values used in the GHG emission reduction calculations. The sampling plan 
design is based on the CDM Guideline: Sampling and surveys for CDM project activities and 
programmes of activities, version 4.

Parameter values may be estimated by sampling in accordance with Sampling Standard for a single 
or a group of PIs36. A single sampling plan covering a group of PIs is justified when either the 
homogeneity of included PIs relative to the parameters of interest can be demonstrated or the 
differences among the included PIs is taken into account in the sample size calculation.

The target population is the combined unique entries of ICS users by PI in the monitoring database 
from which the sample is being drawn.

For each survey, the sampling method is determined by using a random sample of the total 
population of distributed ICS from records generated in the monitoring database and based on the 
precision requirements listed above, and as required by the methodology and guidance in the 
Sampling Standard.

The sample size for each monitoring activity will be the total number of ICS distributed and included 
in the monitoring database. A sample size calculation sheet will be used to calculate the number of 
samples.
Oversampling will be conducted to ensure that the required level of precision is met.

The Sampling Frame will be the monitoring database which may contain information from multiple 
PIs and therefore allows for sampling to be taken per PI or as a group of PIs.

Field-based monitoring activities to determine monitored parameter values will be either a field 
survey, KPT or WBT.

Data shall be recorded for each activity either directly onto a smartphone-based app designed for 
the purpose, or via paper forms where this is not possible.

Once collected, data will be submitted directly from the field to the TASC SA Carbon Project Manager 
for QA/QC and entry into the Monitoring Report.

The TASC SA Carbon Project Manager will have overall responsibility for the implementation of 
the monitoring plan.

Data collection will be conducted by a dedicated monitoring team of trained individuals, either from 
TASC SA or the Project Instance Implementer. The monitoring team will use a survey 
questionnaire and instruments required for KPT/WBT measurements on the sampled ICS.

In order to minimize sampling errors, such as non-responses and errors, the field team will 
practice over-sampling from the population to ensure a total number respondents that meets the 
required level of precision. This will ensure the integrity of the sample group and maintains the 
randomness of participant selection. All sample groups will be re-selected for each monitoring 
period / year, as appropriate for the parameter in question.

If the required level of precision is not achieved, then further surveys may be completed or the 
lower bound value adopted in the calculations.

Where a survey may not be completed, or where there is a non-response, the reasons shall be 
clearly documented in the survey questionnaire.

Completed survey questionnaires and KPT/WBT data will be collected by the monitoring team and 
delivered to the TASC SA Carbon Project Manager for analysis. These shall be checked through 
for errors and completeness, and compiled into a monitoring report. Any incomplete or missing 
data shall be documented clearly. The monitoring report will include:

• 
Summary of activities undertaken, at which location and on which dates

• 
Calculation of the parameter values to be utilized in emissions reduction calculations

The implementation of this monitoring plan will be the responsibility of the TASC SA and its 
specifically trained monitoring team. This team will comprise local operatives who are conversant 
in local languages and customs of rural South Africa. Individuals will be selected based on their 
competence and experience for each monitoring activity, and trained accordingly. Training records 
will be maintained.

There will be no incentives provided for these individuals for the type of data provided, to prevent 
any conflict of interest.

According to the Global Forest Watch platform, 
South Africa lost 1.48 Mha of tree cover from 2001 
to 2020, equivalent to a 25% decrease in tree 
cover since 2000. The Global Forest Watch also 
reported that in 2020 alone, South Africa lost 
30.3kha of natural forest.18 
 
Although South Africa’s forestry sector is well

poor in South Africa on forest resources is

woodlands2. The unsustainable harvesting of

desertification. The annual deforestation rate in 
South Africa is estimated to be 0.2 percent.” 19
